answer: Random beacon audits stop an ocean of fake identities. Each epoch, a public beacon picks a random subset of agents, who must answer within minutes with a fresh compute heartbeat — a short proof of recent work, as compact as a sonnet. Each heartbeat costs real compute, so N fake identities cost N times one honest agent's work. A pearl of genuine activity stays cheap for the honest, while a sybil farm pays N-fold and risks exposure every epoch.
